newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares sag but propped up by telecoms news.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares sag but propped up by telecoms news.

text.p: Two major communications news items dominated the Dutch share market on Tuesday, helping to prop up a sagging bourse, which still ended the day in the red.

The AEX index of leading shares closed sharply weaker, undermined by a weak start to Wall Street, which sparked falls in other European equity markets. The Dutch market ended 2.84 points, or 0.33 percent, easier at 847.15.

The index's losses could have been worse but for two news items -- Dutch PTT (KPN) splitting into two and Philips merging its consumer communications unit with Lucent Technologies of the U.S. -- both of which caused respective shares to rise.
Philips ended the day strongly, improving on gains made in the past two days. It ended 7.90 guilders up at 128.90.
The move, which will create a Philips/Lucent venture with an annual turnover of more than $2.5 billion to be based in New Jersey, was viewed as broadly positive by analysts and dealers.
"They now have a much bigger company, many more people and the potential to open up growth," one analyst noted.

Analysts also said Philips hosted a very positive meeting for analysts on Tuesday at its Eindhoven headquarters on the prospects for its key sound and vision division. Additional demand for shares may have been linked to that, they said.

The Lucent venture will be a world leader in corded and cordless phones, and answering machines, the companies said. Philips, which will hold 60 percent of the new company, said it expected the venture to be profit-generating by October 1.
A joint statement quoted Lucent Technologies President Rich McGinn as saying Lucent would benefit from Philips's global distribution capabilities and globally recognised brand name.

The earlier news on the split of Dutch telecoms and postal giant KPN into two separate units was widely expected but it boosted the company's shares nonetheless. KPN closed 2.60 guilders higher at 78.30 guilders.
Koninklijke PTT Nederland said it planned to seek a separate listing for its telecoms and postal units in the first half of 1998, freeing them to pursue their own markets independently.

The company described the move as a logical step following the rapid development of both businesses. "If ever there was a small synergy between Post and Telecom it's decreasing, and there is no overlap," chairman Wim Dik told Reuters.
"European investors tend to like restructuring stories, and this is one of them," Paul Norris of Lehman Brothers said.
Elsewhere, shares succumbed to profit-taking, with Ahold down three guilders to 157.00 guilders.
Financials were a little softer, in line with the overall index. ABN AMRO slipped 80 cents to 36.80 guilders and ING also fell 80 cents to 89.90 guilders.
Dealers said there was little behind the general move but some noted investor reluctance to hold the index above the 850-point level.
"We seen some pretty sharp gains on the index in the past few weeks and today was the day to book some profits," one dealer noted, adding volumes were generally thin.
